paragraphs: Marimekko is a very famous design company from Finland. 75 years ago, it started making clothes, sheets, and dishes with bright colors and big, bold patterns.

The company started after World War II to bring color to a grey world. At first, people didn’t know how to use these strange, bright fabrics. So, the founder made a fashion show to show them beautiful dresses, and people loved it. Marimekko became world-famous in 1960 when Jackie Kennedy wore one of their dresses on a magazine cover.

The designers get their ideas from nature and small community gardens in Finland. Today, Marimekko is a big part of Finnish life. Almost every person in Finland has something from this brand at home because the bright patterns help quiet people show their happy side.

paragraphs: The famous Finnish design company Marimekko has been adding bright colors and bold patterns to fashion and housewares for 75 years.
In Finland, where spring arrives late, designers find their inspiration in nature and local community gardens.

Maija Louekari draws many abstract illustrations that are later printed onto millions of meters of fabric. The name Marimekko means Mary’s dress, and represents an everyday woman. Founded by Armi Ratia after World War II, the company initially struggled because its patterns were too bold. To help people imagine how to use the fabrics, Ratia organized a fashion show, which became an immediate success.

The brand received a massive global boost in 1960 when Jackie Kennedy wore a Marimekko dress on a magazine cover. Today, the brand is a core part of Finnish identity, and almost every Finnish home owns at least one Marimekko item. This allows naturally quiet people to express their colorful side through their clothes.
